name: Mískito
catalog_quote: Stress is on the initial syllable:'El accento prosódico en miskito recae prácticamente siepre en la primera sílaba de la palabra' (Miskitu bila asainka:25).All exceptions are due to morphological structuring.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Salamanca 1988 quotations are verbatim in the PDF we hold; only the page locator needs correcting (p. 46 and pp. 46-47, not 45 / 45-46; p. 64 correct). (2) Deciding source: a 380-pp MIT PhD grammar (1988) by the principal Miskito specialist, Glottolog's best grammar; its stress remarks are incidental but unambiguous (main stress on the leftmost vowel; vowel length and [h] licensed only there), and the same author's 2008 typological overview (downloaded, Letras 43:104) states flatly 'no hay tonos y el acento está siempre en la primera sílaba'. No phonology article or instrumental study of Miskitu stress is listed in Glottolog or CrossRef. sources.quote: Community/orthographic study (109 Wangki and Tawira speakers, interviews) arguing against strict initial stress: p.34 'La ortografía acentual del idioma miskitu es regida por un sistema de acentuación bifonética en el que afectan a las dos primeras sílabas de la palabra'; p.35 'Los hablantes tawira como los wangki han demostrado que además de llevarla en la primera tonal existe otras palabras que acentúan en la segunda sílaba tónica' (examples mayá, winá vs wina, kupia, tiara; long vowels, diphthongs and closed first syllables keep stress initial). It also quotes the grammar tradition verbatim
